title: GPU econ alternate-metric proforma (tokens/J & $/1M)
body:
Purpose:
This worksheet captures an alternate framing for GPU instance benchmarking that focuses on energy-normalized metrics (tokens per Joule) and a straightforward $/1M-tokens proforma. The goal is to have a compact, comparable view across A10, L4, A100, and H100 for making instance-mix and provisioning recommendations in Optimize and for Dedicated sizing conversations.

Quick notes / methodology: 
- Measurements are synthetic throughput numbers (tokens/s) from microbench harness (small autoregressive model proxy, 1k context, mixed batch sizes representative of bursty web workloads). These are NOT final production numbers; they are normalized probes for relative comparison.
- Power is the steady-state GPU draw measured on PCIe power probe on each instance under steady streaming load. We apply a datacenter PUE multiplier (1.2) to convert raw electricity into facility-level cost.
- Cost assumptions (amortized): GPU allocation cost per hour is a blended internal list-price/reserved estimate (includes infra overhead). Electricity price used = $0.12 / kWh. Small host/network overhead = $0.05 / hr (amortized).
- Output metrics: tokens/s, power (W), tokens per Joule (equivalently tokens/s per W), tokens per hour, total $/hr (GPU + elec + infra), $ per 1M tokens.
- Purposefully include rough margins and rounding; this is a draft used to reason about tradeoffs rather than a final audit.

Table: alternate-metric proforma (single-GPU baseline numbers)

Columns: instance | throughput (tok/s) | gpu_power (W) | tokens/J | tokens/hr | cost/hr (gpu+elec+pct overhead) | $ / 1M tokens

A10 | 12,000 tok/s | 250 W | 48 tokens/J | 43.2M tok/hr | $0.786 / hr | $0.0182 / 1M
L4  | 9,000 tok/s  | 150 W | 60 tokens/J | 32.4M tok/hr | $0.572 / hr | $0.0176 / 1M
A100| 30,000 tok/s | 350 W | 85.7 tokens/J | 108.0M tok/hr | $3.100 / hr | $0.0287 / 1M
H100| 42,000 tok/s | 400 W | 105 tokens/J  | 151.2M tok/hr | $6.108 / hr | $0.0404 / 1M

Interpretation / highlights: 
- Energy efficiency (tokens/J): H100 > A100 > L4 > A10 in this probe set. H100 gives the best tokens per Joule (approx 105 tokens/J) largely due to higher throughput scaling with power.
- $ / 1M tokens: L4 and A10 appear cheapest per token in this narrow proforma because of much lower hourly GPU amortization. A100 and H100 have higher $/1M despite higher tokens/J because the hourly amortized GPU cost dominates.
- Tradeoff: if raw energy cost (electricity) were the dominant component, H100/A100 would win. In practical hosted/reserved pricing, GPU amortization is the bigger driver — hence cheaper-VM classes can often be lower $/token despite worse Joule efficiency.

Normalized perf/W (tokens/s per W) - quick reference: 
- A10: 48 tokens/s/W (baseline)
- L4: 60 tokens/s/W (+25% vs A10)
- A100: 85.7 tokens/s/W (+79% vs A10)
- H100: 105 tokens/s/W (+119% vs A10)

Scenario sketches (recommended allocations):
- Price-sensitive preferrers (multi-tenant embeddings, batching-friendly workloads): prioritize L4/A10 pools. They give the lowest $/1M in our proforma.
- Throughput-first (high-concurrency inference, low SLO tail latency needs): A100 pools may be better due to higher absolute throughput and predictable performance; H100 for the highest tail-sensitive services or for very large models where kernel availability matters.
- Energy-constrained edge/colocated DCs: use tokens/J as the primary objective — prefer H100/A100 if you pay for electricity at scale and GPU amortization is fixed.

Operational considerations / caveats: 
- These numbers do not account for model-specific memory constraints (larger context or FP16/8 quantization may change perf and power characteristics).
- For batched workloads, latency-SLO-driven autoscaling changes effective utilization; effective $/token can drop significantly with improved utilization and caching (prefix/KV).
- Cooling and networking topology can change effective PUE by ±10–30% in edge/colocated settings; redo electricity calc if PUE differs.
- Spot vs reserved pricing: if a customer can use spot for non-critical workloads, adjust GPU amortization downward (examples: A100 reserved $3/hr vs spot $1.2/hr — would shift $/1M materially).

Recommendations / next steps (short):
1) Run the same harness across the canonical model suite (gpt-small proxy, gpt-medium, 4k-context models) and produce a per-model deltas sheet. Ticket: JIRA-RED-2187.
2) Add two more columns: "quantized delta" (perf and power change when running 4-bit) and "batched effective util" (expected util at typical 95th p99 arrival patterns).
3) Produce an instance-mix cost simulator (input: target p50/p95 latency, workloads QPS/time-of-day, model family) that outputs a recommended pool mix (L4/A10 + burst to A100/H100) and monthly $ estimate.
4) Validate GPU hourly amortization against Finance (role: Tobias Nguyen) — our blended numbers are intentionally conservative; get actual committed price points for Dedicated customers.

Notes to self (informal): 
- The $/1M numbers are compellingly low for L4/A10 — need to check empirical model fidelity. Could be the proxy model underestimates memory stalls.
- Check the harness for FP16 vs FP32 toggles; older runs had an accidental FP32 fallback which shifted perf numbers by ~10%.

Unresolved questions: 
- For customers on Reserved Dedicated, do we pass through GPU amortization linearly or apply a utilization uplift credit? (Product ops question)
- How to fold per-token quality regressions into the econ model (i.e., cost to switch to a cheaper model vs revenue/retention impact)?

Appendix: quick calculation examples (A10):
- tokens/hr = 12,000 * 3600 = 43,200,000
- raw elec $/hr = (0.25 kW * $0.12/kWh) = $0.03 -> after PUE(1.2) = $0.036
- total $/hr = GPU(0.70) + elec(0.036) + infra(0.05) = $0.786
- $ / 1M tokens = 0.786 / 43.2 = $0.0182

References / links: see linked_artifacts above for the playbook and the benchmark PR.

Next sync: I'll push a version with per-model deltas by 2025-02-09 and request review from applied-ml and product-optimize.

(End of draft — this is a working spreadsheet-style doc, expect rough edges and follow-ups.)
